gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-khmer: Visitor draws every stroke like solder pulled through a nozzle, flat and unmodulated, with gaping mouths on its e. And Noto Sans Khmer, a sans-serif with small letters standing proud, brings generous openings that make it the livelier half of the pair.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Visitor is nostalgic and digital, with short ascenders over big bowls and a monoline skeleton. Noto Sans Khojki keeps its exits wide enough to pass light through, so a longer passage would feel open and unhurried.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-khudawad: Nostalgic and a bit digital, Visitor looks traced with a marker, all gaping mouths and short ascenders. And Noto Sans Khudawadi, approachable and sans in build, does the quieter work of keeping its rounds unlatched and its capitals close to lowercase height.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-kr: Chunky, pixel-era lettering with plain, unshaded lines. Visitor supplies the retro punch up top, while Noto Sans KR, a sans-serif with a big x-height and stubby ascenders, carries the text below with generous gaps in its curves.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-lao: Visitor sets horizontals as thick as its verticals, with gaping e mouths and short ascenders for a nostalgic, digital look. Noto Sans Lao, a sans-serif with a tall x-height and open mouths on c, e and a, does the steadier work of carrying text.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-lao-loop: Noto Sans Lao Looped reads as solid blocks, not skylines. Visitor tops it with gaping e mouths and bars of identical thickness, so a nostalgic display heading sits over a sans-serif body with bowls left unfinished on one side.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-lepcha: Nostalgic through and through, Visitor cuts every stroke to one width and gapes wide on its e. Noto Sans Lepcha holds a lowercase with the stature of cast iron capitals, and Visitor earns its keep when big and brief.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Nostalgic and digital, Visitor pulls a monoline stroke from start to finish, with big bowls under short ascenders. Noto Sans Limbu, a sans-serif with tall-bodied small letters and gaping curves, handles the reading.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-lydian: Noto Sans Lydian is approachable, with capitals barely taller than lowercase. Visitor's ruler-drawn line and gaping e mouths make a nostalgic heading, so give it generous size and let the sans below it stay modest.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-mahajani: Noto Sans Mahajani stands tall, its lowercase towering over the capitals. Visitor's constant pen pressure and gaping e mouths feel nostalgic up top, while the sans below, with its funnel-like throat on the e, would read smoothly across a longer passage.
